questions.stem: A hand lens helps you see small things closely.
questions.explanation: A hand lens makes small things look bigger. We use it to look closely at a leaf, an ant or a seed.

questions.stem: Match each tool to its job.
questions.explanation: A ruler measures length. A hand lens helps us look closely. A thermometer shows how hot or cold. A timer shows how long something takes.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order. What does a scientist do first? Then?
questions.explanation: A scientist asks a question, makes a guess, tests it, records what happens and then tells other people.

questions.stem: To find which ball bounces highest, we drop every ball from the same height.
questions.explanation: Dropping every ball from the same height makes the test fair. Then only the ball is different.

questions.stem: In a fair test, we keep things the ___.
questions.explanation: In a fair test we keep things the same. We only change one thing.

questions.stem: How do young scientists stay safe? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: We listen to our teacher, wash our hands and ask before we smell anything. We never taste things in a test, and we do not run around.

questions.stem: Which tool would you use? Sort each job.
items: how tall a bean plant is
how long sand takes to fall
questions.explanation: A ruler measures length and height. A thermometer measures how hot or cold. A timer measures how long something takes.

questions.stem: Before the test, Mina says: 'I think the rubber ball will bounce highest.' What is this?
questions.explanation: A prediction is a good guess about what will happen. A result is what we see after the test.

questions.stem: Look at the thermometers. Which one shows the hottest?
questions.image_alt: Three thermometers A, B and C. A is at 12 degrees, B at 37 degrees and C at 48 degrees.
questions.explanation: The red line goes highest on thermometer C. A higher line means hotter.

questions.stem: Which tool measures how long a book is?
questions.explanation: A ruler measures how long something is. The stopwatch is for time, the thermometer is for how hot, and the balance scale is for how heavy.

questions.stem: Sort the tools. Which ones measure? Which ones help you look closely?
questions.explanation: Rulers, thermometers and stopwatches give us numbers. Hand lenses and microscopes make tiny things easier to see.

questions.stem: Look at the thermometers. Put them in order from hottest to coldest.
questions.image_alt: Three thermometers A, B and C. A shows 5 degrees, B shows 25 degrees and C shows 40 degrees.
questions.explanation: The line is highest on C, so C is the hottest. B is in the middle. The line is lowest on A, so A is the coldest.

questions.stem: Nadia drew these pictures each week. The tadpoles grew into frogs.
questions.image_alt: Life cycle of a frog: eggs, tadpole, froglet, adult frog.
questions.explanation: Nadia looked closely and drew what she saw. The picture shows eggs, then tadpoles, then froglets, then adult frogs.

questions.stem: Which part of your body helps you see what a leaf looks like?
questions.explanation: We use our eyes to see. Looking closely is one way to find out about things.

questions.stem: Mina and Raju race toy cars down a ramp. Mina pushes her car. Raju lets his car go. Is it a fair test?
options: No. Mina pushed her car and Raju did not.
Yes. Both cars are on the same ramp.
Yes. Both children are in Class 1.
questions.explanation: Mina pushed, so her car got a head start. A fair race lets both cars go the same way.

questions.stem: Nadia sees tiny black wriggly things in the village pond. What does a young scientist do?
options: Guess a name and stop looking.
Look closely and draw what she sees.
questions.explanation: Scientists look closely and record what they see. We never taste things to find out, and one guess is not enough.

questions.stem: At home, Joy finds a bottle of coloured liquid in the kitchen. He wants to know what it is. What is the safe choice?
options: Ask a grown-up and do not touch it.
questions.explanation: Some liquids are dangerous. We ask a grown-up and never smell, taste or touch things we do not know.

questions.stem: Tuli wants to know how tall her bean plant is. She measures it with a ___.
questions.explanation: A ruler measures how tall or how long something is.

questions.stem: Class 1 dropped three balls. Why did they drop every ball from the same height?
questions.model_answer: To make it a fair test. The height was the same for every ball.
questions.explanation: If one ball was dropped from higher up, we could not tell why it bounced higher. Keeping the height the same makes the test fair.

questions.stem: Match each science step to an example.
pairs: I think the big stone will sink.
questions.explanation: A question starts an investigation. A prediction is a guess before the test. We record what we see and then share it.

questions.stem: Class 1 dropped balls from the same height. Bounce in hand spans: rubber ball 6, tennis ball 4, football 3. The ___ bounced the lowest.
questions.explanation: The football has the smallest number, 3, so it bounced the lowest. The rubber ball bounced highest with 6.

questions.stem: Class 1 dropped balls from the same height. Bounce in hand spans: rubber ball 6, tennis ball 4, football 3. How much higher did the rubber ball bounce than the tennis ball?
questions.explanation: 6 take away 4 is 2. The rubber ball bounced 2 hand spans higher than the tennis ball.

questions.stem: Tuli tests two paper planes. She throws plane A very hard and plane B gently. Plane A flies further. What should she change?
options: Throw plane B even more gently.
Throw both planes in the same way.
questions.explanation: Tuli threw the planes differently, so we cannot tell if the plane or the throw made the difference. Throwing both the same way makes it fair.

questions.stem: Joy grows two bean plants in the same kind of pot. Plant A is in the sun and gets water. Plant B is in a dark cupboard and gets no water. Which things are different? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: The water and the light are different. Because two things changed, Joy cannot tell which one made plant B small. A fair test changes only one thing.
